new_docs.provider: Outlook Business (via screener wire, Anarock data cited within)
new_docs.claims_summary: Dubai H1 2026 residential transactions AED 225.7bn, +15% vs H1 2024 but -16% vs H1 2025; prices softened 4-7% Feb-Apr amid regional conflict then recovered; Anarock calls it sentiment-driven, not structural; full-year 2025 record AED 547bn / 206,166 transactions.

entry_orbs.why: Dubai residential transaction volume and price-per-sq-ft are the market-level backdrop for EMAAR's development-sales revenue, which revenue-drivers models as volume x price x mix.
The article frames the move as geopolitical/macro-cycle risk to the Dubai residential market, which is the external variable external-dependency tracks for EMAAR's development exposure.

new_docs.claims_summary: UAE construction cost index +5.2% YoY in Q1 2026 (raw materials +8-9%, block works +25%); copper +12% YoY and crude oil +13% YoY cited as drivers; Abu Dhabi Chamber projects a further 4.5% construction-cost rise in 2026; example given is contractor Alec Holdings, whose energy-division margin fell to 2.9% from 8.7% — no EMAAR-specific figure is cited; developers described as shifting toward higher-margin luxury projects to protect returns.

entry_orbs.why: Sector-wide input-cost inflation (materials, labour, block works) is exactly the input-cost / commodity-cost margin-driver category margin-drivers models, but the article names a contractor (Alec Holdings) as its evidence, not EMAAR, and gives no EMAAR-specific cost or margin figure.

The article names copper, oil, steel and aluminium price moves as the drivers of UAE construction-cost inflation, which is the commodity-exposure variable external-dependency tracks for a developer's build-cost base.
